title: Numerical Solution of Equations Module 2 Lesson 2: Iterate and Justify Accuracy custom practice

evidence_basis.originality_note: All prompts, values and combinations are original; mapped Cambridge evidence informs scope and assessment structure only.

parts.prompt:
The sequence of values given by the iterative formula
$$x_{n+1} = \sqrt[3]{3x_n + 5}$$
with initial value $x_1 = 2$, converges to the real root of the equation $x^3 - 3x - 5 = 0$.

Calculate the values of $x_2$ and $x_3$, giving each value correct to 4 decimal places.

Use the iterative formula
$$x_{n+1} = \ln(x_n + 4)$$
with initial value $x_1 = 1.7$, to determine the root of the equation $\mathrm{e}^x - x - 4 = 0$ correct to 2 decimal places. Give the result of each iteration to 4 decimal places.

Working in radians, use the iterative formula
$$x_{n+1} = \dfrac{1}{3}\left(\cos x_n + 4\right)$$
with initial value $x_1 = 1.3$, to find the root of the equation $3x - \cos x - 4 = 0$ correct to 2 decimal places. Give the result of each iteration to 4 decimal places.

It is given that the equation $\mathrm{e}^x + 2x - 8 = 0$ has a root $\alpha \approx 1.58$.

By evaluating the expression $\mathrm{e}^x + 2x - 8$ at two suitable values, show that $\alpha = 1.58$ is correct to 2 decimal places.

Use the iterative formula
$$x_{n+1} = \dfrac{1}{2}\left(5 - \ln x_n\right)$$
with initial value $x_1 = 2$, to determine the root of the equation $2x + \ln x - 5 = 0$ correct to 2 decimal places. Give the result of each iteration to 4 decimal places.

The equation $x^3 - 5x - 4 = 0$ has a root $\alpha \approx 2.6$.

By evaluating $x^3 - 5x - 4$ at suitable values, show by calculation that $\alpha = 2.6$ is correct to 1 decimal place.

questions.prompt: The equation $x^3 - 4x - 1 = 0$ has one positive root $\alpha$.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt:
Use the iterative formula
$$x_{n+1} = \sqrt{4 + \dfrac{1}{x_n}}$$
with initial value $x_1 = 2$, to determine $\alpha$ correct to 2 decimal places. Give the result of each iteration to 4 decimal places.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: By evaluating $f(x) = x^3 - 4x - 1$ at two suitable values, show that $\alpha = 2.11$ is correct to 2 decimal places.

questions.prompt: The equation $(x + 2)\mathrm{e}^x = 7$ has a single real root $\alpha$.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt:
Show that the equation $(x + 2)\mathrm{e}^x = 7$ can be rearranged into the form
$$x = \ln\left(\dfrac{7}{x + 2}\right)$$
and use this iterative formula with initial value $x_1 = 0.8$ to find $\alpha$ correct to 2 decimal places. Give the result of each iteration to 4 decimal places.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: By evaluating $f(x) = (x + 2)\mathrm{e}^x - 7$ at suitable values, justify that $\alpha = 0.89$ is correct to 2 decimal places.

questions.prompt: The equation $2\tan x - 3x - 1 = 0$ has a root $\alpha$ in the interval $0 < x < \dfrac{\pi}{2}$.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt:
Working in radians, use the iterative formula
$$x_{n+1} = \arctan\left(\dfrac{3x_n + 1}{2}\right)$$
with initial value $x_1 = 1.0$, to find $\alpha$ correct to 3 decimal places. Give the result of each iteration to 5 decimal places.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: By evaluating $f(x) = 2\tan x - 3x - 1$ at the boundaries of a suitable interval, justify that $\alpha = 1.148$ is correct to 3 decimal places.

questions.prompt: The positive root of the equation $x^3 = \ln(x + 5)$ is denoted by $\alpha$.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt:
Use the iterative formula
$$x_{n+1} = \sqrt[3]{\ln(x_n + 5)}$$
with initial value $x_1 = 1.2$, to find $\alpha$ correct to 3 decimal places. Give the result of each iteration to 5 decimal places.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: By evaluating $f(x) = x^3 - \ln(x + 5)$ at suitable values, prove that $\alpha = 1.223$ is correct to 3 decimal places.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: State whether the sequence of iterates in part (a) converges monotonically (staircase pattern) or oscillatingly (cobweb pattern), giving a reason based on the values of $x_n$.

questions.prompt: The equation $3\sin x = \mathrm{e}^{-x/2}$ has a root $\alpha$ in the interval $0 < x < \dfrac{\pi}{2}$.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt:
Working in radians, use the iterative formula
$$x_{n+1} = \arcsin\left(\dfrac{1}{3}\mathrm{e}^{-x_n/2}\right)$$
with initial value $x_1 = 0.3$, to find $\alpha$ correct to 3 decimal places. Give the result of each iteration to 5 decimal places.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: By evaluating $f(x) = 3\sin x - \mathrm{e}^{-x/2}$ at the boundaries of a suitable interval, justify that $\alpha = 0.292$ is correct to 3 decimal places.

questions.prompt: The equation $x^2\ln(x + 3) = 15$ has a single positive real root $\alpha$.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt:
Use the iterative formula
$$x_{n+1} = \sqrt{\dfrac{15}{\ln(x_n + 3)}}$$
with initial value $x_1 = 3.0$, to determine $\alpha$ correct to 3 decimal places. Give the result of each iteration to 5 decimal places.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: By evaluating $f(x) = x^2\ln(x + 3) - 15$ at suitable values, prove that $\alpha = 2.906$ is correct to 3 decimal places.

questions.prompt: The equation $2x + \ln(x^2 + 1) = 4$ has a unique positive root $\alpha$.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt:
Use the iterative formula
$$x_{n+1} = \dfrac{1}{2}\left(4 - \ln(x_n^2 + 1)\right)$$
with initial value $x_1 = 1.5$, to find $\alpha$ correct to 3 decimal places. Give the result of each iteration to 5 decimal places.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: By evaluating $f(x) = 2x + \ln(x^2 + 1) - 4$ at suitable values, confirm that $\alpha = 1.439$ is correct to 3 decimal places.
